messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I guess  new to almost everything here.

But I need to build a R WEB base app for my finale project at school.

I'm using UBUNTU 10.10 on a Dell vostro 1500 .

I installed apche and R sucsesfully.

I'm using this guide :http://rapache.net/
manual.html#Configuring_rapache

Trying to install rapache , but I'm new to UNIX...

I think that:

./config
make
make install

Work OK.

Now I'm stuck at this step in the guide:

3. Configuring rapache

When i type:
jonhs@ubuntu:/$ LoadModule R_module

This is the output:
LoadModule: command not found

I guess i should RUN it from a folder? Which one?

I hope it is not a problem that I erase the "rapache-1.1.14.tar.gz"
directory after running:

./config
make
make install

I will be grateful for some help for beginners...

Thanks,

yoni.

messages.subject: Re: Installing rapache first time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yonatan,

LoadModule R_module is not a bash command. It's an Apache directive that loads the module. If you're using Ubuntu, you need to edit apache2.conf (/etc/apache2/apache2.conf, though I'm not quite sure about the file path).

Anyway, go to the module section of that file, you'll see a bunch of similar entries, then just paste "LoadModule R_module     <path to module>" after that block. After compilation, R module file (mod_R.so) should be in "modules" folder. Provide a path to a file in a system folder, NOT the one you have in your extraction folder. And yes, you can delete that folder. It's not needed after compilation, but it occupies less than 10MB, it's not that much, and it has an offline manual, tests, tools... IMHO it's not a good practice to delete an extraction folder after compilation. =/

Hi yonatan,
                  I dont know whether ur problem is solved or not, yeah me to tried different ways to configure rapache but I figured it as simple as possible.

If u already installed Ubuntu, u can go through this process

R installation on Ubuntu
     - search in Synaptic Package manager for r-base or type the command in the terminal as sudo apt-get install r-base

Apache2 installation
    - sudo apt-get install apache2

Rapache installation
     - from package .deb, which is provided in this link:  http://ppa.launchpad.net/jeffreyhorner/rapache/ubuntu/pool/main/liba/libapache2-mod-rstats/  or search in software center for libapache2-mod-rstats

Thats it, every thing is all set - only thing we have to do some changes in apache configuration

In my case, I typed the code in the terminal sudo etc/apache2/apache2.conf to get the configuration file and then add the folloeing lines code in the conf file.

<Location /RApacheInfo>
	SetHandler r-info
</Location>

<Directory /var/www/R-files>
	SetHandler r-script
	RHandler sys.source
</Directory>

then try with a simple .R code in R-files folder, u will definitely get the result

Next thing to do is installing brew - u might be facing problems with brew installation

For installing brew, go to terminal and change the permissions of the following folder as R through apache directly checks the the following folder for the packages

sudo chmod a+rwx /usr/local/lib/R/site-library

then go to R through terminal and install the brew package using the code

install.packages("brew", lib="/usr/lib/R/site-library")

then go to sudo etc/apache2/apache2.conf file  and copy paste the code

<Directory /var/www/brew>
	SetHandler r-script

	RHandler brew::brew
</Directory>

Now in that brew folder go with that example in jeroens lecture.

i hope everything works fine, if not plzz reply..

right now I am all set with above procedure but facing problems with javascript handling, I hope u can help me out

perhaps you meant: sudo gedit /etc/apache2/apache2.conf

<Directory /var/www/brew>

	RHandler brew::brew

Just navigate your browser to W3Schools and read the tutorial, it's quite straightforward... http://www.w3schools.com/ajax/default.asp I don't prefer the mashup of HTML and R, since it's too cumbersome for bookkeeping, so use separate files for R scripts. Jeroen mentioned something about IE incompatibility with .rhtml files, just search the mailing list. I really don't have a bloody idea what's happening within IE when it encounters a .rhtml file. However, you can use "" directive and set some kind of prefix to your R scripts (like Jeroen did in ggplot webapp, just watch the NET panel in Firebug upon form submission), then match the scripts with regular expression. By doing such, you won't mess up the plot file retrieval. If you set brew::brew to operate on all files in a directory, you're probably not going to see the desired result, since you practically tell Apache to use R to process the png file. You don't want that, right? The main idea is that you should asynchronously call R script (that's what's AJAX is all about), and load desired content. You can use JSON to serialise the data (e.g. table data and png file location), there's RJSONIO package available on CRAN: www.omegahat.org/RJSONIO/ Just don't, I repeat DON'T do the layout stuff with R, use JS instead. You can set data.frame, working directory and plot path in a list, then wrap it inside toJSON, something like this: require(RJSONIO) g <- read.csv(FILES$FirstFile$tmp_name, header=T) g_head <- head(g) setwd("/var/www") wd <- getwd() plot_file <- "bglot.jpg" fpath <- file.path(wd, plot_file) res <- list(file_preview = g_head, working_directory = wd, plot = plot_file) png(fpath) # do the plotting stuff... dev.off() toJSON(res) # you should wrap this up in several functions, FWIW Once you return JSON from AJAX call, you can massage the data with JavaScript. It can be a bit labour-intensive, but you shouldn't do that within R, use JS to render the stuff on the client side, and leave computations for the server side (R scripts). Oh, and try using some JS library to make your life easier (jQuery or ExtJS), but first, get a firm grasp on JS "per se"! In that case, you don't need brew, you can easily use sys.source. Anyway, try naming your R scripts systematically (and leave the extension, put in the prefix): rscript-one rscript-two Here's an example config file (use .htaccess, not the global conf) SetHandler r-script RHandler base::sys.source REvalOnStartup "library(RJSONIO)" ROutputErrors Good luck, have fun! messages.body_plain:
Hi Yonatan,

I reckon that you've already installed & configured RApache correctly. Try to replicate /RApacheInfo example from the official manual.

Now, if you're familiar with R, read man pages for brew and Sys.source functions. You should only use brew (IMHO) if you're trying to embed R code chunks in HTML. In that case, you use ASP/PHP-like tags <% %> to separate R code from HTML.

If you're not familiar with web-development, I recommend you to put RApache on hold for a while, and read tutorials on w3schools.com <http://w3schools.com> - they are free and easy to understand. Start from HTML and CSS, and continue with JavaScript and AJAX. IMHO, PHP is not essential for building RApache-powered webapp.

Anyway, I'm not sure I understand "how to send variables to a server" part... RApache gets the data from HTTP request such as POST and GET, and creates POST and GET objects - lists, to be precise. Read the RApache manual, but get familiar with basic web-development techniques first.

LoadModule log_config_module  modules/mod_log_config.so

/usr/sbin/apachectl configtestLoadModule log_config_module ../../../usr/lib/httpd/modules/mod_log_config.so

Unfortunately, my knowledge of this is fairly limited and my memory of the process is pretty fuzzy, but hopefully something in the thread or my notes will help you figure out what's going on.  On the bright side, I did eventually get everything working!

LoadModule R_module modules/mod_R.so
<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

Then do /etc/init.d/httpd restart.

 -Harlan

messages.subject: Re: An error with RApache
messages.body_plain:
Hi Prashantha,

Looks like your configuration is calling the "LoadModule" directive
too many times. Scope out the files in /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/ and
see if it's not getting called there.

Also, RLibrary is not a valid directive for rApache. You could rewrite that as:

REvalOnStartup "library(GDD)"

Scope out http://www.rapache.net/manual.html for more info.

One more note: I would suggest using another graphics device besides
those found in GDD. The Cairo package is better. And also don't rule
out just using png(type='cairo') if png is all you need.

Best,

Jeff
